fields.Text: C++20 {{c1::concepts}} constrain template parameters with named, checkable requirements, giving much clearer compiler errors than std::enable_if/SFINAE.

constexpr marks a function/variable that {{c1::MAY}} be evaluated at compile time (falls back to runtime), while consteval marks an "immediate function" that {{c2::MUST}} be evaluated at compile time.
CMake's {{c1::CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE}} setting controls optimization: Debug adds symbols and disables optimization, while Release enables optimizations and strips debug info.
fields.Extra: Why use CMake at all? It's a cross-platform build-system generator — one CMakeLists.txt can produce Makefiles, Ninja files, or IDE projects on Linux/macOS/Windows, and it manages dependencies and flags consistently.

fields.Front: Write a C++20 function template constrained to only accept integral types using a concept.
fields.Back:
template <std::integral T>
T add(T a, T b) {
    return a + b;
}

fields.Front: Write a C++20 ranges pipeline that filters a vector of ints for even numbers, then squares them.
fields.Back:
auto result = nums
    | std::views::filter([](int n) { return n % 2 == 0; })
    | std::views::transform([](int n) { return n * n; });

fields.Front: Which three keywords, if any one appears in a function body, make that function a C++20 coroutine?
What's the main build-system benefit of C++20 modules over textual #include headers?
fields.Back: Faster compilation (no re-parsing headers per translation unit) and no macro/preprocessor leakage between files — imports are isolated, not textually pasted in.

fields.Front: What operator does C++20 add for three-way comparison, and what is it commonly called?
fields.Back: <=>, the "spaceship operator" — a single overload can generate <, >, <=, >= automatically.

fields.Front: Write a C++20 struct that gets all six comparison operators for free using the spaceship operator.
fields.Back:
struct Money {
    long cents;
    auto operator<=>(const Money&) const = default;
};
A lightweight, non-owning view (pointer + length) over a contiguous sequence — works over arrays, vectors, etc. without copying data.

BMO's C++20 financial calculation engine cut transaction batch-processing latency by how much, and across how many daily account records?
fields.Back: 42% latency reduction across 2.5M+ daily account records.

fields.Front: What macro defines the entry point pybind11 uses to build a Python extension module from C++?
fields.Back: PYBIND11_MODULE(module_name, m) — m is the module object you attach functions/classes to.

fields.Front: Write a minimal pybind11 snippet exposing a C++ function "add" to Python.
fields.Back:
#include <pybind11/pybind11.h>
namespace py = pybind11;

int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }

PYBIND11_MODULE(fastmath, m) {
    m.doc() = "fast C++ math functions";
    m.def("add", &add, "Add two integers");
}

fields.Front: Which pybind11 template class exposes a C++ class to Python, and how do you bind a method with it?
Why must pybind11 code explicitly release the GIL before running a long, CPU-bound C++ computation?
fields.Back: By default the GIL stays held during the C++ call, blocking every other Python thread. Releasing it lets other Python threads run concurrently while the C++ work executes.

Write the minimal CMakeLists.txt to build a C++20 executable named "app" from main.cpp.
fields.Back:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(app LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

add_executable(app main.cpp)

fields.Front: What does target_link_libraries(target PRIVATE dep) do, and what does the PRIVATE/PUBLIC/INTERFACE keyword control?
fields.Back: Links `dep` into `target` and propagates its include dirs/compile flags; PRIVATE = used only inside target's own build, PUBLIC = also propagated to anything that links target, INTERFACE = propagated but not used by target itself.
